description: Figure 4 is a horizontal bar chart illustrating the number of participants (N=6) who identified each of seven evaluation criteria as beneficial in a user study. The vertical axis lists the criteria in descending order of participant count: “Relevant FCs” (6 participants), “FC Summary” (5), “Relevance Explanation” (3), “Clarity and Simplicity” (3), “Overall Summary” (2), “Filters” (1), and “Veracity Explanation” (1). The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of Participants,” is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 2. Each criterion is represented by a distinct horizontal bar, with its length proportional to the number of participants who selected it; the bars are color-coded, with “Relevant FCs” in dark purple, “FC Summary” in medium blue, “Relevance Explanation” in teal, “Clarity and Simplicity” in green, “Overall Summary” in light green, “Filters” in olive green, and “Veracity Explanation” in lime green. The chart visually emphasizes that “Relevant FCs” was the most valued feature, while “Filters” and “Veracity Explanation” were the least selected, each chosen by only one participant.
